review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

10:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ συνπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
10:1.targetText: Then Jesus left that place and went into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds came to Him and He taught them, as was His custom.

groups.note: συνπορεύονται ("came together") is N1904's spelling of συμπορεύονται.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB sets "beyond the Jordan" beside Judea with a comma instead of rendering καί ("and").
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering καί.
BSB renders only the first πάλιν ("again"); the second, with ἐδίδασκεν, is not repeated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle ἀναστάς.
English joins the participle ἀναστάς, rendered "left", to "went".

10:2.sourceText: Καὶ προσελθόντες Φαρισαῖοι ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.
10:2.targetText: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.

groups.note: The participle πειράζοντες ("testing") expresses purpose, rendered "to test".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the opening καί.
BSB leaves αὐτόν ("Him") after ἐπηρώτων implicit.
εἰ ("whether") introduces the question, which BSB gives as direct speech.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; γυναῖκα has no pronoun.

10:3.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς;
10:3.targetText: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the pronoun "he".
ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") implicit.

10:4.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι.
10:4.targetText: They answered, “Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away.”

groups.note: The article οἱ with δέ works as the pronoun "they".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the unstated subject of the infinitives "to write" and "send away".
English supplies the unstated recipient of the certificate.
English supplies the object of ἀπολῦσαι.

10:5.targetText: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; ἔγραψεν gives it only in the verb ending.

10:6.targetText: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; ἐποίησεν gives it only in the verb ending.

10:7.sourceText: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα,

groups.note: ἔσονται εἰς ("will be into") is a Semitic idiom for "will become".

10:14.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με, μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά· τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.

10:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτά.

groups.note: ἐναγκαλισάμενος ("taking in the arms") is rendered "took ... in His arms".
The one αὐτά ("them") is the object of both ἐναγκαλισάμενος and κατευλόγει; BSB renders it "the children", then "them".
The article τάς has possessive force here.
